source_refs.claim: Source facts in lines 32-46: held-out probe accuracy previously coexisted with null steering; coherence, separation, causal patch upper bounds, and dose curves are required before treating a direction as controllable.
Source facts in lines 52-65: the P0 primary criteria include signed target action/logit effect and random-control separation, with INSTRUMENT_INVALID when discrimination or random control fails.

Source facts in lines 74-105: the reliability screen requires direction coherence, class separation, signed per-sample effect, reverse-effect, dose/collapse, already-correct damage, and robustness before more complex control.

caveats: A positive logit intervention is evidence about the bounded frozen substrate and target-token readout, not proof of user-visible behavioral benefit or PE validity.
No reader, threshold, model binding, evaluator, or runtime configuration is changed by this topic.
topic.demand_relevance: Directly tests the Steerable axis and the demand's causal connection to the frozen model's next-token decision, including signed target-logit improvement and separation from a matched random direction.
falsification_signals: No non-random reader produces a positive held-out signed target-logit effect, or the sign is inconsistent across views.

The matched random direction has an indistinguishable effect, or the target effect disappears on held-out wording, format, language, role-order, or counterfactual views; classify causal instrument validity as failed.
Positive average effect is accompanied by excessive reverse effects, correct-to-wrong flips, or collapse under the bounded patch.
topic.hypothesis: Causal hypothesis: a readable direction that lies in the downstream causal subspace will improve the signed target-token margin under a bounded residual patch across held-out views, while a norm- and layer-matched random direction will not.
topic.mechanism: Source facts: the corpus records a prior case where held-out probe accuracy coexisted with null steering and requires direction coherence, class separation, causal upper-bound patching, dose curves, and random-control separation. Test mechanism: patching a consumed residual direction should change the next-token logit in the intended sign; the matched random patch isolates generic norm or perturbation effects.
topic.research_question: Does any specified non-random reader produce a bounded, cross-view, signed target-token logit effect that exceeds the matched random-direction effect?
success_signals: At least one non-random reader produces a positive signed target-token margin improvement on held-out identities and every required view.
The target effect exceeds the matched random-direction effect by the frozen separation threshold, with coherent sign and a bounded dose-response curve.
Already-correct damage, reverse effects, and collapse remain below their frozen limits while the effect is retained outside the original view.
topic.suggested_method: Using only reader directions selected from the training side, freeze each direction and apply the same bounded residual patch to matched held-out examples. Compare strict noop, each non-random reader direction, and random directions matched for layer, position, norm, and dose. Stratify by semantic identity and view; preregister dose and sign analyses. Measure paired target-token margin change, confidence intervals, per-sample signed effects, reverse-effect rate, already-correct damage, and collapse indicators without using evaluation or human scores as learning signals.
topic.title: Causal target-logit effect versus matched random direction
